title: tuistory PNG screenshot renderer does not reflect per-cell ANSI color in this terminal chain -- P6.1 color-level claims are UNVERIFIED, not FAIL
methodology_followed: 1. Positive control: focus-border glyph swap (thick <-> thin box-drawing) on WORKTREES/DIFF panels -- capture pipeline correctly registered this text-content change (different sha256, PIL diff bbox non-None). Confirms the pipeline CAN detect real changes.
2. Re-verified active theme via TEXT before drawing conclusions: settings panel showed 'cyberpunk ACTIVE' explicitly before capture; this is app-state ground truth independent of pixel rendering.

3. Attempted raw ANSI/SGR inspection two ways: (a) tuistory snapshot --fg/--bg color filters -- returned EMPTY for every color tested, including definitely-present black/white, proving the filter itself is non-functional in this environment, not informative about app color; (b) independent raw capture via `script -F` wrapping the actual app directly (bypassing tuistory entirely) with TERM=xterm-256color and COLORTERM=truecolor forced -- captured 7681 real bytes of app output containing ZERO SGR color escape sequences of any kind (neither truecolor 38;2;r;g;b nor 256-color 38;5;n forms), despite the app successfully booting past its own isTTY check.

4. Palette-distance check with CORRECTED hex values (my first attempt in this session had used synth's hex values by mistake for cyberpunk -- corrected here): cyberpunk (#FF6B35 accent) vs ice (#38BDF8 accent) quantize to meaningfully different 256-palette indices (203 vs 75) and remain visually distinct even under maximum color-tier degradation. Re-checked amber vs ice for a maximally distant pair: also clearly distinct (214 vs 75). Palette collision is definitively ruled out as an explanation.

5. Direct pixel-content audit of EVERY captured PNG this run (not just theme-comparison pairs): every single PNG -- across proofpunk-agent, awesome-researcher, and this scratch gates run, spanning both P5 and P6 phases -- contains only 31-37 unique colors, ALL of which are exactly tuistory's documented --background default (#1a1b26) and --foreground default (#c0caf5) plus their anti-aliasing blends. Zero instances of any app theme's declared border/accent/ok/err/warn/info hex values (or their 256-quantized snaps) appear in ANY captured PNG.
conclusion: The app IS correctly applying theme state (proven via text: toast fired, ACCOUNTS/THEME panel labels and ACTIVE marker updated instantly, settings persist). However, NO instrument available in this driving session (tuistory PNG screenshot, tuistory --fg/--bg filters, or a raw `script`-based byte capture under this environment's PTY chain) can observe the app's actual per-cell ANSI color output. This is a genuine, reproducible instrument limitation specific to this terminal/harness chain (tmux-nested PTY), not a demonstrated app color-application defect and not a demonstrated app color-application success -- the color dimension of P6.1 is simply unobservable here.
p6.1_corrected_verdict: UNVERIFIED (color dimension only) -- the capture pipeline available in this session cannot discriminate the two color states, so P6.1 cannot be graded PASS or FAIL on color evidence. The non-color dimension of P6.1 (theme selection state applies instantly across the app, confirmed via settings-panel text and toast) is PASS.
not_filed_as_new_defect: This is NOT filed as an aperant-tui application defect (no F-15 app bug) because all evidence points to the measurement instrument (tuistory's PNG renderer + its --fg/--bg filters, and this session's script-based raw capture) failing to expose color, not the app failing to emit it. Per the driver-not-fixer mandate, no source was touched; this is reported as an instrument/environment limitation for the operator to weigh.
what_instrument_would_resolve_this: Either: (a) a tuistory version/mode confirmed to read per-cell SGR from its internal buffer rather than applying fixed default colors in PNG conversion, verified against a KNOWN-colored ANSI fixture before trusting it on this app; or (b) driving the app in a real (non-nested, non-tmux) terminal emulator with a screenshot tool that reads the terminal's actual rendered pixels (e.g. a native terminal app under macOS Screenshot, not a PTY-buffer-to-PNG converter); or (c) instrumenting the app itself (out of scope for a driver) to log the resolved hex/ANSI codes it computes per render so they can be diffed as text.
